docs.text: Welcome to Nicole's Lab! Lesson Summary (April 13, lesson25) In this lesson, we started to use the new software for 3D modeling, modifying and refining the previously designed box and UNO bottom box. We all gradually mastered the finer operations in modeling, laying the foundation for the next structural combinations. In the next lesson, we will continue to complete the design and printing of the UNO box, and then formally enter the learning module of motion structure.

I have been able to translate the structural features of electronic components into corresponding fixtures and achieve accurate modeling.

docs.text: Welcome to Nicole's Lab! Lesson Summary (February 23, lesson20) In the course, I completed the installation of Rhino 3D modeling software, and learned operations such as view switching, basic model creation and editing. After the lesson, I organized the recent learning content into a review document, which is convenient for daily review and consolidation. From next week onwards, I will gradually go deeper into complex modeling techniques, and I will review the content in the document more often in my spare time.

docs.text: Welcome to Nicole's Lab! Lesson Summary (March 2, lesson21) In this lesson, we learned the basic concepts of 3D printing, including its principles, developmental origins, and application scenarios, and the teacher helped us build a comprehensive understanding of 3D printing technology. Then, we learned how to use 3D printing slicing software and explored publicly available 3D modeling websites to understand how to obtain and prepare models for printing. In the end, I successfully printed my favorite 3D model and experienced the complete process from digital model to physical object!

docs.text: Welcome to Nicole's Lab! Lesson Summary (March 23, lesson22) In this lesson, we learned about the concept of tolerances and how to control the fit between parts in the design and manufacturing process. Then, we learned the modeling techniques of Rhino software, including the method of creating surfaces from plane curves, and the union and difference operations in Boolean operations. In the practical session, we completed a box with a lid through Rhino modeling and learned how to do skeleton design.

docs.text: Welcome to Nicole's Lab! Lesson Summary (March 30, lesson24) In this lesson, we continued our in-depth study of tolerance, analyzing and adjusting the boxes printed in the previous lesson to optimize them for tolerance problems. We also reviewed Boolean operations and strengthened our understanding and use of union and difference sets. In the hands-on session, we modeled and created a simple box for UNO.
